summary.objective: Decide whether to retain and investigate the current J12 connector or evaluate a replacement, without changing the board pinout.
summary.headline: Two synthetic shift notes conflict on board revision (Rev C vs Rev D) and event count (three vs five); neither is established as authoritative and no vibration or retention data exists.

anchors.excerpt: Controller board revision on the affected unit: Rev C.
Three J12 disconnect events were logged during vibration on the test track.
No vibration-test result or retention measurement is attached to this note.
Controller board revision on the affected unit: Rev D.
Five J12 disconnect events were logged during vibration on the test track.
This note does not reference shift note A and does not explain the difference.
No vibration-test result or retention measurement is attached to this note.

knownFacts.statement: Note A records the controller board revision on the affected unit as Rev C.
Note B records the controller board revision on the affected unit as Rev D.
Note A states three J12 disconnect events were logged during vibration on the test track.
Note B states five J12 disconnect events were logged during vibration on the test track.
Note B does not reference note A and does not explain the difference.
Neither note has a vibration-test result or retention measurement attached.

alternatives.title: Retain and investigate the current J12 connector
alternatives.description: Keep the existing J12 connector and pinout while reconciling the conflicting records and gathering physical evidence on the disconnect mechanism.
prerequisites: Confirm the actual board revision of the affected unit
Reconcile the event count from primary logs
Obtain vibration profile and retention measurements

alternatives.title: Evaluate a replacement connector
alternatives.description: Evaluate a replacement connector that preserves the existing board pinout and drive controller footprint (author-entered constraint). Compatibility is unknown until evidenced; no candidate part is identified in the sources.
prerequisites: Confirm pinout and footprint compatibility with evidence

affectedArtifacts.label: J12 connector on the drive controller board
affectedArtifacts.basis: Both notes report J12 disconnect events.

affectedArtifacts.label: Controller board revision record (Rev C / Rev D)
affectedArtifacts.basis: Inference: the revision record must be corrected once the authoritative revision is established.

affectedArtifacts.label: Test-track disconnect event log
affectedArtifacts.basis: Inference: event count differs between notes, so the primary log needs review.

evidenceGaps.gap: Conflict: board revision recorded as Rev C (note A) vs Rev D (note B); no authoritative record identified.
evidenceGaps.whyItMatters: The baseline and footprint/pinout constraints cannot be confirmed without knowing the revision.

evidenceGaps.gap: Conflict: three (note A) vs five (note B) disconnect events; the difference is unexplained.
evidenceGaps.whyItMatters: Failure frequency drives the severity assessment and choice between alternatives.

evidenceGaps.gap: No vibration-test result, vibration profile or retention measurement is available.
evidenceGaps.whyItMatters: Without physical evidence the root cause and any replacement suitability cannot be assessed.

evidenceGaps.gap: Unknown whether the notes describe the same unit, the same run, or overlapping events.
evidenceGaps.whyItMatters: Inference: the notes may be counting different or overlapping event sets.

reviewQuestions.question: Which board revision (Rev C or Rev D) is physically on the affected unit?
reviewQuestions.prerequisite: Physical inspection of the unit's board marking

reviewQuestions.question: What do the primary test-track logs show for the number of J12 disconnect events?
What vibration profile and retention measurements are required before any connector change is considered?
Who authored notes A and B and do they refer to the same unit and runs?

nextAction.action: Physically confirm the board revision of the affected unit and reconcile it against both notes before selecting an alternative.
nextAction.requiredInput: Board marking inspection of the affected Rover Alpha unit

limitations: Packet ready means the paid preparation artifact was delivered. It is not engineering approval, a completed test or permission to release hardware. Independent engineering review and relevant physical evidence remain required.
All sources are labeled synthetic fixtures invented for demonstration; statements are cited as synthetic fixture content.
Neither note is treated as authoritative; conflicts are recorded as evidence gaps.
The pinout/footprint constraint is author-entered from the brief (SYN-REQ-v1 is not in the frozen manifest).
